correctness.rationale: Explicit graph isomorphism to a two-row twisted ladder is checked. For m>=5 every distance<=2 pair is captured by a rung, adjacent-column support disjointness, or same-row distance-two inequality. A four-clique gives χ>=4. Four-color support complementarity forces c_{i+2}=swap(c_i); twisted closing forces m≡2 (mod4), and the period-four construction proves sufficiency. M6²=K6 and M8²=K8. For M16², a square-independent four-set would occupy every other column with three interior row alternations and an incompatible twisted seam, implying alpha<=3 and χ>=6; an explicit six-color word meets it. Three checked five-color seeds at m=5,7,12 and a rigorously verified length-four insertion cover the other residue classes. The packaged direct-graph verifier replays all explicit words, hundreds of lengths and all four-element subsets at m=8. Finite computations are supporting checks, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The claim classifies a whole natural cubic vertex-transitive family newly motivated by the 2026 3-dynamic/square-coloring framework. Sharp four-color rigidity, the exceptional sixteen-vertex six-color case, and an explicit five-color insertion scheme resolve exact behavior that is not deduced from prior broad bounds or the untwisted prism answer. It is a substantive infinite-family classification with a structural explanation, not an arbitrary isolated computation.
